This document
outlines the inspection checklist I2, which 
must be carried out every 3 months 
as indicated by M3 in the above title block. 
The 
first draft has been 
initiated by eng. El-Sayed 
Abdel Moneam El-Geddawy and 
tested at 19 May 2002 for charger no.1 at Sheraton El Matar 66kv Substation, Cairo zone.

Input voltage 3*380 v AC, 
Output voltage 220 v DC, Output current 50A DC

Input voltage tolerance + 
15%, Input frequency tolerance + 5%

Wearing goggles, safety shoes, helmet, and rubber gloves 
 is necessary

items:
Work order must be issuedand 
 the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,

Normal operation of the charger is putting it on AUTOMATIC POSITION. In this 
 case it must charge the battery with floating (normal) charging voltage

For a power failure of a period < 5 minutes, the 
 charger will remain in FLOAT mode on return of power

For a power failure of a period > 5 minutes, the 
 charger will automatically switches to the HI-RATE mode, when power returns 
 and continue for a period before returns to FLOAT (according to the adjustable 
 period)

To check the previous characteristics, switch of 
 the power supply of the charger for a period < 5 minutes (e.g. 4 minutes), and 
 observe (after switching on power supply) that the charger continued working 
 in FLOAT mode

Check the operation FLOAT voltage using 
 digital DC voltmeter (must be 245 v 1 %)

Then switch of the power supply of the charger 
 for a period > 5 minutes (e.g. 6 minutes) and observe (after switching on 
 power supply) that the charger transferred to HI-RATE mode

Check the operation HI-RATE voltage using digital 
 DC voltmeter (must be 253.75 v 1 %)
 Turn off Charger and Then:

Repeat maintenance steps that performed monthly 
 according MPIS doc no. Ch-010-r0

Check wire connections and be sure that there is 
 no loosing

Check general conditions of the charger such as 
 gaskets, vents, etc

Clean the charger (from inside and outside) using 
 blower

Substations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document
outlines the inspection checklist I2, which 
must be carried out every 3 months 
as indicated by M3 in the above title block. 
The 
first draft has been 
initiated by eng. El-Sayed 
Abdel Moneam El-Geddawy and 
tested at 19 May 2002 for charger no.1 at Sheraton El Matar 66kv Substation, Cairo zone.
The Charger technical data:
Input voltage 3*380 v AC, 
Output voltage 220 v DC, Output current 50A DC
Input voltage tolerance + 
15%, Input frequency tolerance + 5%
Safety 
Precautions
Switch off the power supply,
No smoking is permitted,
Wearing goggles, safety shoes, helmet, and rubber gloves 
 is necessary
Work order must be issuedand 
 the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,
Tools and Equipments
Digital voltmeter
Suitable tool 
 set
Vacuum Cleaner or blower
Brush
Work to be carried out
Normal operation of the charger is putting it on AUTOMATIC POSITION. In this 
 case it must charge the battery with floating (normal) charging voltage
For a power failure of a period < 5 minutes, the 
 charger will remain in FLOAT mode on return of power
For a power failure of a period > 5 minutes, the 
 charger will automatically switches to the HI-RATE mode, when power returns 
 and continue for a period before returns to FLOAT (according to the adjustable 
 period)
To check the previous characteristics, switch of 
 the power supply of the charger for a period < 5 minutes (e.g. 4 minutes), and 
 observe (after switching on power supply) that the charger continued working 
 in FLOAT mode
Check the operation FLOAT voltage using 
 digital DC voltmeter (must be 245 v 1 %)
Then switch of the power supply of the charger 
 for a period > 5 minutes (e.g. 6 minutes) and observe (after switching on 
 power supply) that the charger transferred to HI-RATE mode
Check the operation HI-RATE voltage using digital 
 DC voltmeter (must be 253.75 v 1 %)
 Turn off Charger and Then:
Repeat maintenance steps that performed monthly 
 according MPIS doc no. Ch-010-r0
Check condition of internal components
Check wire connections and be sure that there is 
 no loosing
Check general conditions of the charger such as 
 gaskets, vents, etc
Clean the charger (from inside and outside) using 
 blower
